newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares close higher in line with Europe.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares close higher in line with Europe.

text.p: 1720 GMT - Portuguese shares closed higher in sympathy with European markets, lifted by the strength of the dollar. Trade in Portugal Telecom, cement group Cimpor and Banco Totta e Acores (BTA) accounted for 60 percent of the bourse turnover of 11.5 billion escudos.
* Shares in BTA dropped to a low of 3,000 escudos, six percent below yesterday's close, after a press report that Alipio Dias had resigned as president of the bank.
* Some dealers said it was feared that Dias's eventual resignation could signal a break with the bank's past policy of paying out high dividends.
"The sellers are afraid that the departure of Alipio Dias is synonymous with a change in the policy of good dividends," said one dealer.

According to a report in weekly Semanario Economico, Luis Champalimaud, son of the head and founder of the Champalimaud group Antonio, could combine the chairmanship of both of the group's major banks, Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor and Banco Totta.
